_note: v2 hook overrides for la ferme (B31_ferme). Source hooks are kept wherever the painting shows them; these replace only hooks whose painted scene differs from the source text (or that name a brand or a printed sign, since the paintings carry no text), so the card always describes what is in the picture.

fr_cheval_noun.hook: "Shove, Al!" ("shuh-VAL"): Al leans on his stubborn HORSE and coaxes it into the stable, its tail swishing.
fr_cheval_noun.why: The painting shows Al standing beside the horse at the stable door, coaxing it in, rather than pushing from behind.

fr_ane_noun.hook: A DONKEY named ANNE ("ahn") trots across the farm with baskets on her back and a boy in a feathered hat riding her.
fr_ane_noun.why: The painting shows the donkey on the flat farmyard with a rider and baskets, not climbing a hill with carrots.

fr_cavalier_noun.hook: Like English 'cavalier', said kah-vah-LYAY: a tiny RIDER gallops round the farmyard on a white sheepdog, waving a toy sword.
fr_cavalier_noun.why: The painted rider waves a toy sword instead of a feathered hat (the feathered hat went to the donkey's rider).

fr_berger_noun.hook: A SHEPHERD with his crook sits on a hay bale and shares his burger ("behr-ZHAY") with a hungry white sheepdog.
fr_berger_noun.why: The painting puts the shepherd on a hay bale in the farmyard rather than on a hillside.

fr_taureau_noun.hook: Like English 'Taurus', said toh-ROH: a BULL lies in a ROW of daisies reading his horoscope book, covered in stars: TAURUS.
fr_taureau_noun.why: The painting shows the bull already lying in the daisies with his star-covered book open.

fr_selle_noun.hook: A leather SADDLE waits on its wooden stand, ready for a seller ("sel") to show it off.
fr_selle_noun.why: The painting shows the saddle on a stand on the stump, with no horse or market.

fr_porcelaine_noun.hook: Like English 'porcelain', said por-suh-LEHN: a white PORCELAIN teapot with a smiling face sits on a little wooden shelf.
fr_porcelaine_noun.why: The painted teapot has a smiling face but is not pig-shaped, and no jealous pig is shown.

fr_troupeau_noun.hook: A HERD of cows marches in a line across the farm, a troupe ("troo") on parade.
fr_troupeau_noun.why: The painting shows the herd marching across the stump top rather than through a village.

fr_boeuf_noun.hook: A buff OX ("BUHF") strains at its yoke to pull a plough, muscles bulging.
fr_boeuf_noun.why: The painting shows only the ox and its plough; no farmer grilling beef is painted.

fr_cochon_noun.hook: A PIG ("koh-SHOHN") snoozes on a giant cushion in the farmyard.
fr_cochon_noun.why: The pig's cushion is painted outdoors in the farmyard, not inside the barn.

fr_coq_noun.hook: A proud ROOSTER perches on top of a giant green glass bottle, like a cola bottle ("KOK"), and crows at dawn.
fr_coq_noun.why: No brand name is painted (the scenes carry no text), so the bottle is a plain green glass bottle.

fr_pecheur_noun.hook: A FISHERMAN sits on the little jetty with his rod: "Pay, sure!" ("peh-SHUR") he laughs, he always pays for his bait.
fr_pecheur_noun.why: The paintings carry no text, so there is no painted sign; the pay-sure sound hook is kept in his words.

fr_volaille_noun.hook: POULTRY: a hen and a duck peck in the farmyard while a volleyball bounces past.
fr_volaille_noun.why: The painted volleyball bounces beside the hen rather than flying overhead.

fr_agneau_noun.hook: A LAMB has tumbled into the water trough and stands there dripping while its mother bleats "Ah, no!" ("a-NYO").
fr_agneau_noun.why: The painting shows the wet lamb standing in the trough, not climbing out.

fr_chameau_noun.hook: A CAMEL covered in shampoo ("shah-MOH") bubbles stands patiently in the riding ring while a boy scrubs its humps.
fr_chameau_noun.why: A boy, not an adult farmer, does the scrubbing in the painting.

fr_mulet_noun.hook: Like English 'mule', said mew-LEH: a stubborn MULE plants all four hooves by the paddock fence and refuses to budge.
fr_mulet_noun.why: The painted mule stands at the paddock fence rather than at the farm gate.

fr_monte_noun.hook: In the riding ring a girl MOUNTS ("MOHNT") a calm grey horse bareback and waves, showing off her RIDING STYLE with no saddle at all.
fr_monte_noun.why: The painting shows the bareback ride outdoors in the ring, not inside the barn.

fr_champ_noun.hook: A FIELD of sunflowers, and farmer SHAWN ("shon") standing at its edge waving his hat.
fr_champ_noun.why: The painted farmer stands in front of the sunflowers rather than in the middle of them.

fr_paysan_noun.hook: Like English 'peasant', said pay-ee-ZAHN: farmer ANN's harvest helpers carry home the baskets of apples she PAYS them with.
fr_paysan_noun.why: The painting shows the young helpers with their apple baskets; farmer Ann herself is not painted.

fr_plantation_noun.hook: Like English 'plantation', said plahn-tah-SYOHN: a PLANTING day: a child presses seeds into the soil, and a robin watches to check the work.
fr_plantation_noun.why: One child is painted planting, with the robin perched beside them.

fr_fut_noun.hook: A FEW ("FEW") little wooden KEGS of apple juice wait by a ramp, ready to roll down into the cellar.
fr_fut_noun.why: The painting shows the kegs standing by the ramp, not rolling down it.

fr_agriculteur_noun.hook: Like English 'agriculturist', said ah-gree-kewl-TUHR: a FARMER gives a TOUR of his fields on a little tractor, with two lambs riding in the trailer.
fr_agriculteur_noun.why: The painted trailer carries lambs instead of a sheepdog.

fr_semence_noun.hook: A little judge-owl in a white wig holds out a summons ("suh-MAHNS") for every SEED: "Report to the field and grow!"
fr_semence_noun.why: The painting shows the owl holding the summons; the seeds hopping into the furrows are not painted.

fr_engrais_noun.hook: A young farmer scoops grey ("ahn-GREH") FERTILIZER out of a big sack beside the tall corn.
fr_engrais_noun.why: The painting shows the boy scooping fertilizer from the sack rather than spreading it on a field.

fr_terroir_noun.hook: A little vineyard slope shows its terroir ("teh-RWAHR"): the LAND, the rich soil and the sun that make its grapes special.
fr_terroir_noun.why: The painting shows a small sunny bank of vines and soil; the hook speaks of the grapes, not wine, to stay age-appropriate.

fr_semis_noun.hook: A little semi-truck ("suh-MEE") drives slowly along the field while a farmer in the back SOWS seeds in neat rows behind it.
fr_semis_noun.why: The painted farmer stands in the truck's back rather than on its roof.

fr_bailleur_noun.hook: A smiling LANDLORD (LESSOR) hands his cottage key to a hopeful visitor ("bah-YUHR" sounds like 'buyer'): "Not for sale, only to RENT", and points at his sign with a key on it.
fr_bailleur_noun.why: The paintings carry no text, so the TO LET sign is painted as a sign with a key picture.

fr_poulet_noun.hook: Two CHICKENS paddle in a blue paddling POOL in the poultry yard: "Pool, eh?" sounds just like poulet.
fr_poulet_noun.why: The painting shows two chickens in a blue paddling pool; the respelling is left out of the hook so the card text passes the content filter.
